meta.usage_note: Each function entry carries signature, description, and structured detail to varying depth depending on doc_status: "full" (has a dedicated wiki page — the richest entries, including since/compatibility/example_code where the page states them), "full_demo_confirmed" (no wiki page, but signature and description are confirmed via the bundled bBox Plug-in Demo.fmp12 file's own embedded function-reference text and/or the compiled plugin binary's internal Do_* handler table — solid primary-source evidence, just thinner detail than a wiki page provides), and "stub_no_wiki_page" (reconstructed only from indirect cross-references — the least certain tier; verify against beezwax.net or the demo file before relying on one for precise parameter-by-parameter guidance). doc_bug_note fields flag upstream documentation errors (typos, copy/paste artifacts) found in either the wiki or the demo file during this build.
meta.known_gaps:
"bBox Text Window Action" and "bBox Text Window Open" were excluded from the v1.0 build as unverified (they appeared only in a third-party draft, bbox-plugin-skill.json, found in the beezwax/bbox-documentation repo root). That exclusion was corrected in a same-day review after obtaining the actual bBox_1.06_FMP_plug-in download (Developer-provided): both are genuinely real, confirmed independently via the bundled bBox Plug-in Demo.fmp12 file's own embedded function-reference text and the compiled plugin binary's internal Do_TextWindowAction handler. Both are now catalogued in the 'AppleScript and macOS Automation' category. "bBox Select Menu Item" is likewise now catalogued as bBox_SelectMenuItem, confirmed the same way. 

A second "bBox Perform Script" entry in the wiki's own (duplicate-riddled) Script Step List remains uncatalogued — no signature, description, or cross-reference for it exists anywhere, including in the demo file; it's likely just a list duplicate rather than a distinct feature. 

The compiled plugin binary (bBox.fmplugin/Contents/MacOS/bBox) also contains internal Do_* handlers with no confirmed public bBox_ name or signature in any available source (wiki, third-party draft, or demo file text): Do_AppleMapsWebSnapshot, Do_ListFields, Do_ListTables, Do_GitOpen, Do_CutTextCharacters, Do_CutTextFields, Do_SQLiteExecMany, and Do_DuckDBOptions (the latter almost certainly bBox_DuckDBOptions, parallel to bBox_SQLiteOptions, but not catalogued without a confirmed signature). These are real, compiled-in features — not phantoms — but deliberately not catalogued with an invented signature. Test them directly in FileMaker (bBox_ListFields(), bBox_ListTables(), etc. are reasonable first guesses given the internal naming convention) or check beezwax.net before relying on any of them.
meta.update_instructions: Re-run the fetch+parse pass periodically: 1) clone the wiki repo (git clone https://github.com/beezwax/bbox-documentation.wiki.git) rather than scraping rendered HTML — the wiki has no releases API, so there's no tag-based drift signal like goya-be-plugin or claris-filemaker-pro use; page presence/absence and content are the only signals available. 2) Diff the cloned page list (`git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only`) against this catalog's entries to find additions/removals — do this via git's object listing, not a plain `ls`, since the wiki repo's mixed-case filenames collide on a case-insensitive macOS volume during checkout (confirmed while building v1.0: several bBox_* files silently didn't appear in a case-insensitive `ls` despite being present in the git history). 3) For new/changed pages, parse the **`function( params )`** heading, the Parameters/Result/Error/Script Step code block, then the prose below the second `***` divider for description/notes/examples. 4) Re-check the bBox_LastError reference table in Errors-&-Troubleshooting.md for the function list this catalog treats as 'stub' — if a function gains its own page, promote it to a full entry. 5) Check https://github.com/beezwax/bbox-documentation for whether the current version (1.06 as of this build) has changed — Home.md's '### Current Version' section is the only version signal since there's no releases API; cross-check against the Related Blog Posts list for a newer numbered post. 6) Treat the repo-root bbox-plugin-skill.json (if still present) as a lead-finder only, never as authoritative — it had a JSON syntax error (trailing comma) and several entries with less parameter detail than the wiki pages themselves provide. 7) If a fresh plugin download becomes available (a bBox_X.XX_FMP_plug-in folder containing Documentation/, per-OS binaries, and the bBox Plug-in Demo.fmp12 file), it's a genuinely valuable second source, confirmed in this same-day review: run `strings -n 6` on the demo .fmp12 file and grep for `bBox_` — its layouts embed a full function-reference text index (name, signature, description) that is NOT the same content as the wiki and catches real gaps (this pass found bBox_Sort missing entirely, several stub signatures that were wrong or incomplete, e.g. bBox_FileWrite's missing `unzip` parameter, and about 15 functions with no wiki presence at all, like the bBox_HTTP_* family). Also run `strings -n 4` on the compiled plugin binary itself (macOS/bBox.fmplugin/Contents/MacOS/bBox) and extract Itanium-mangled `_ZDo_` symbols (slice exactly N characters starting right after the digits, using Python — a plain regex under-matches because the mangled suffix length varies) to get the internal handler list; cross-check against confirmed bBox_ names to find internal-only functions with no public signature yet (see meta.known_gaps for the current list). Read Info.plist's CFBundleVersion for the precise build number (e.g. 1.06.7, more specific than the wiki's bare "1.06"). Don't fabricate a signature for an internal-only Do_ name found this way — list it in known_gaps instead, exactly as this pass did. 8) https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-functions is a THIRD real source — an older ("0.97+"-era, pre-1.06) function index whose ~60 entries mostly overlap the wiki (same broken links, e.g. bBox_DuckDBExec/Open both mislinking to the old bbox-sqlite* pages from before DuckDB replaced SQLite) — but each name links to its own dedicated page (https://www.beezwax.net/{lowercase-name-no-underscores}, e.g. bbox-sqliteclose, bbox-sort, bbox-doscript, bbox-sysctl) in the SAME rich format as a wiki page (Parameters/Result/Error/Script Step block, First appeared/Examples/Compatibility, prose description). A FULL SWEEP of this source was completed the same day it was discovered: all ~60 unique linked pages were fetched (`curl -A "Mozilla/5.0"`, no auth needed) and parsed (the page format is consistent enough for a single regex-based extractor — see the retrieval method below), then diffed against every matching catalog entry by name and by rough parameter count. 6 linked URLs (the whole bBox_WebView* family) returned HTTP 302 to /404 — genuinely absent from this older source, not a fetch failure; the WebView family is presumably a post-"0.97+" addition. Of the ~54 pages that did resolve, about 20 catalog entries gained real corrections: since/compatibility fields the demo file hadn't provided, richer prose descriptions, and in a few cases outright behavioural facts absent from every other source (bBox_DoScript is NOT PSoS-compatible and runs asynchronously; bBox_FileRead/FileWrite/FileStatus/FileSymLink all warn that their path parameter is a literal value — don't escape or quote it; bBox_SQLiteOpen's own docs note it was slated for replacement by bBox_DuckDBOpen in 1.05). One GENUINE, UNRESOLVED CONFLICT was found and deliberately left unresolved rather than silently picked: bBox_PythonEval's demo-file signature (1.06-era) is `(reference; expression)`, session-based, but this older page (since 0.84) describes a materially different 1-parameter, session-less `(expression)` version — see its doc_bug_note for the full writeup; don't trust either without testing directly in FileMaker. Retrieval method for a future re-sweep: extract the {name: url} map from the index page's `bBox_Name(...)` anchors, curl each unique URL, and parse each page's Parameters/Result/Error/Script Step block plus the "First appeared in / Examples in demo file / Compatibility" line and the prose after the final divider. Treat any conflict with the demo file (1.06-era, generally the newer source) in the demo file's favour, but still record the older page's detail as a note rather than discarding it, per the bBox_DoScript `control`-parameter and bBox_PythonEval examples above.

Shell, Bash, and Zsh.notes: The three POSIX shell functions share a mode-flag vocabulary (see shared_reference.mode_flags) and all report errors via bBox_LastError("posix"). bBox_Shell only returns stdout and does not accept container data as its script parameter; bBox_Bash and bBox_Zsh support container field references (see shared_reference.container_field_references) and finer input/output control. macOS now defaults to Zsh, and its bundled Bash is far behind Linux's, so prefer bBox_Zsh on macOS.

bBox_Shell.name: bBox_Shell
bBox_Shell.description: Executes the given text with the Unix shell and returns stdout only (max 2 GB, truncated after 160 MB). Does not support container data as the script parameter; for more control over input/output use bBox_Bash or bBox_Zsh instead.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = convert both input/output line endings; 1 = skip CR-to-LF conversion on input; 2 = skip LF-to-CR conversion on output; 3 = don't translate input or output line endings

parameters.name: script
parameters.description: String to be evaluated (executed) by the shell

bBox_Shell.result: String returned after executing the shell command (maximum of 2 GB, truncated after 160 MB)

bBox_Bash.name: bBox_Bash
bBox_Bash.description: Runs text as a Bash script with more control over input/output/parameters than bBox_Shell, including container-data support. A superset of bBox_Shell — supports interpreter command-line options and Bash-only syntax not available in sh.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = convert both line endings, wait for output; 1 = skip CR-to-LF on input; 2 = skip LF-to-CR on output; 4 = don't wait for completion (asynchronous); 32 = combine stdout & stderr

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Input text to be processed
Additional Bash options or parameters (optional)

bBox_Bash.result: stdout from Bash execution (truncated to a maximum of 160 MB)
notes: Supports container field references (see shared_reference.container_field_references).
Bash defaults to the "C" character encoding (ASCII only) — high-bit/multibyte UTF-8 characters can cause problems unless handled explicitly.

bBox_Zsh.name: bBox_Zsh
bBox_Zsh.description: Runs the Zsh shell interpreter, sending text (typically a script) to its stdin, and returning stdout as the function result (truncated to a maximum of 160 MB). macOS defaults to Zsh (its Bash is outdated), so this is generally preferred over bBox_Bash on macOS; Zsh is available but not installed by default on Ubuntu.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Same shared mode flags as bBox_Bash (line-ending and async control)

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Input text to be processed (sent to stdin)
Up to 8 additional parameters to the Zsh command, typically used with -s

bBox_Zsh.result: stdout from Zsh execution (truncated to a maximum of 160 MB)
notes: Supports container field references (see shared_reference.container_field_references).
since/result-limit confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-zsh (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page, 8 demo examples).

bBox_ShellExitStatus.name: bBox_ShellExitStatus
bBox_ShellExitStatus.description: Returns the numeric result code from the last shell command executed (bBox_Shell, bBox_Bash, bBox_Zsh, or the script-step equivalents).
notes: Confirmed via the bBox Plug-in Demo file's embedded function reference — no dedicated wiki page exists for this function.

AppleScript and macOS Automation.notes: macOS-only functions for scripting other applications and simulating UI input. All are limited or non-functional server-side (PSoS/schedules) because there is no accessible logged-in GUI session.

bBox_Applescript.name: bBox_Applescript
bBox_Applescript.signature: bBox_Applescript ( mode ; script {; handler ; param1 ; param2} )
bBox_Applescript.description: Compile and run an AppleScript script, using the script's return value as the function's result. If no return value is given, the result is "?". Can optionally call a specific handler (subroutine) with up to two parameters.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Currently not used

parameters.name: script
parameters.description: A string that will evaluate to a valid AppleScript script

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: Subroutine name that should be called (optional)

parameters.name: param1
parameters.description: First parameter to pass to handler (optional)

parameters.name: param2
parameters.description: Second parameter to pass to handler (optional)

bBox_Applescript.result: String representation of data returned by the AppleScript script
bBox_Applescript.script_step_equivalent: bBox Applescript [ Script; Handler ] — note the script step does not accept parameters, only a handler name
notes: Parameters are encoded as UTF-8, which can be a problem for text needing 16-bit characters; script text and output use UTF-16.
String results are enclosed in double quotes. For a numeric result, wrap the call in GetAsNumber, e.g. GetAsNumber (bBox_Applescript( 0; "(1+1)" )) = 2.
Optional trailing parameters can be omitted while still supplying the handler name.

bBox_ApplescriptLastError.name: bBox_ApplescriptLastError

parameters.description: One or more text parameters with characters to key in

Networking.notes: HTTP/S and file-transfer functions. bBox_Curl has no shell between it and the curl binary, so shell quoting conventions (spaces after an option, etc.) do not apply — see notes.

bBox_Curl.name: bBox_Curl
bBox_Curl.description: Return the results of the curl command with the given parameters. Each FileMaker parameter is equivalent to one curl parameter. Commonly used for REST and SOAP calls.

parameters.name: param1
parameters.description: First curl parameter (required)

parameters.name: param2...
parameters.description: Additional curl parameters (optional, zero or more)

bBox_Curl.script_step_equivalent: bBox Curl [ Param1; Param2; Param3; Param4; Param5; Param6; Param7 ] (version 0.98+)
notes: Since there is no shell involved, there is no space-stripping — write "-o/var/tmp/file.html" rather than "-o /var/tmp/file.html" (which would work in an actual shell).
Long-form option names must be their own FileMaker parameter, e.g. bBox_Curl ("--output"; "/var/tmp/file.html"; "http://beezwax.net").
Quotes generally aren't needed around parameters the way they would be in a shell; GetAsURLEncoded may be needed in some cases.

Download-progress output goes to the system log (macOS) or fmshelper.log (Ubuntu) unless suppressed with -s; -v output goes to stderr, not stdout — use curl's --trace options or add 32 to mode to combine stdout & stderr.
Supports container field references (see shared_reference.container_field_references), e.g. for --upload-file.

bBox_Scp.name: bBox_Scp
bBox_Scp.description: Uses the OpenSSH scp command to copy files from given remote or local sources and destinations. Similar to the cp command, but source/destination can be anywhere reachable via SSH.

parameters.name: param1
parameters.description: First scp parameter

parameters.name: param2
parameters.description: Second scp parameter
Zero or more additional parameters

notes: Use SSH keys for automated usage to avoid needing to supply passwords.
Server-side, scp runs as the fmserver OS account (or fmsadmin group), which must have the needed SSH-key/destination access.
Use the -v option for more debugging output.

Databases (DuckDB and SQLite).notes: bBox 1.05+ uses DuckDB as its embedded database engine; the SQLite functions (bBox_SQLiteOpen/Exec/Options/Close) are documented by the vendor as being for "older bBox versions" and have no dedicated wiki pages — prefer the DuckDB functions in new work. Both engines use an open/exec/close reference lifecycle keyed by a session reference number (see shared_reference for thread-safety notes). bBox_ExecuteSQL is a separate, stateless one-shot query function that targets a file path directly rather than an open reference. bBox_SQLiteImport and bBox_DuckDBRun are registered by the plugin but explicitly marked "Not Implemented" in the vendor's own demo file — don't recommend either. A bBox_DuckDBOptions function also exists internally (the compiled plugin has a Do_DuckDBOptions handler, presumably parallel to bBox_SQLiteOptions) but no confirmed public signature or description was found in any available source — not catalogued here to avoid guessing at one; see meta.known_gaps.

bBox_DuckDBOpen.name: bBox_DuckDBOpen
bBox_DuckDBOpen.signature: bBox_DuckDBOpen ( path {; columnDelimiter ; rowDelimiter ; optionName1 ; optionValue1 ; ...} )
bBox_DuckDBOpen.description: Creates a DuckDB session using the file at the given POSIX path. If an empty string is specified, an in-memory database is used. Returns a reference number greater than 0 if successful.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: POSIX path to the database file, or "" for an in-memory database

parameters.name: columnDelimiter
parameters.description: Optional column delimiter for formatting result text

parameters.name: rowDelimiter
parameters.description: Optional row delimiter for formatting result text

parameters.name: optionName1 / optionValue1 ...
parameters.description: Optional repeating name/value pairs for further DuckDB session options — the demo file's own text was truncated mid-signature at this point, so the exact repeat limit isn't confirmed

notes: This is a materially richer signature than earlier reconstructed — the wiki has no dedicated page for this function at all, and the previous edition of this catalog under-reconstructed it as just `( path {; options} )`. Confirmed via the bBox Plug-in Demo file's embedded function reference, though the trailing optionName/optionValue repeat pattern is cut off in the source text and not fully confirmed.

bBox_DuckDBExec.description: Execute the DuckDB statement(s) against an open reference, using zero or more SQL parameters. Container data is converted to its GetAsText equivalent. SQL may call back into FileMaker via the fmevaluate function, e.g. SELECT fmevaluate ("List (TABLE::field)").

parameters.name: reference

parameters.name: statement

parameters.name: parameters

bBox_DuckDBClose.name: bBox_DuckDBClose

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Session reference returned by bBox_DuckDBOpen

bBox_ExecuteSQL.description: Runs a SQL query directly against a database file path (or "" for the current file) without a persistent open reference. UPDATE, INSERT, and TRUNCATE are supported; CREATE, DROP, and ALTER should also work.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Name of the database file, or "" for the current file

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: A valid SQL expression

parameters.name: columnSeparator
parameters.description: Delimiter for columns in output (defaults to tab)

parameters.name: rowSeparator
parameters.description: Delimiter for rows (defaults to newline)

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: Zero or more SQL parameters (optional)

bBox_ExecuteSQL.result: Text result of the SQL expression, or "?" on error
bBox_ExecuteSQL.script_step_equivalent: bBox Execute SQL [ Expression; Field Separator; Row Separator; Parameter 1; Parameter 2; Parameter 3; Parameter 4 ]
notes: If a record is open on the same table being queried, the query will take longer than usual.
Can be run from any layout and can target another, previously-opened file.
For a JSON array result instead, consider bBox_JavaScript ("fm.executesql ('SELECT ...')"; "JSON") instead.

bBox_SQLiteOpen.name: bBox_SQLiteOpen
bBox_SQLiteOpen.description: Creates a SQLite session using the file at the given POSIX path. If an empty string is specified, an in-memory database is used. Superseded by the DuckDB functions — the vendor's own docs note this function was slated to be replaced by bBox_DuckDBOpen in version 1.05.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: POSIX path to the database file, or "" for an in-memory database

bBox_SQLiteOpen.result: A positive number indicates success and is the session ID
notes: since/compatibility/result/error confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-sqliteopen (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page) — including the explicit DuckDB-replacement note.

bBox_SQLiteExec.name: bBox_SQLiteExec
bBox_SQLiteExec.description: Executes a SQLite3 SQL statement using the session's file. Superseded by bBox_DuckDBExec.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Session reference returned by bBox_SQLiteOpen

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: SQL statement to execute

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.description: Zero or more bind values (optional)

notes: since/compatibility/error confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-sqliteexec (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page, 8 demo examples).

bBox_SQLiteOptions.name: bBox_SQLiteOptions
bBox_SQLiteOptions.description: Sets the column/row separators used when formatting SQLite result sets as text. Use the options parameter to pass one or more SQLite option names, delimited with returns or commas.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Session reference returned by bBox_SQLiteOpen

parameters.name: columnSeparator
parameters.description: Delimiter for columns in output

parameters.name: rowSeparator
parameters.description: Delimiter for rows in output

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional SQLite option name(s), return- or comma-delimited

notes: since/compatibility confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-sqliteoptions (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page) — that page has no prose description beyond the Parameters/Result/Error block.

bBox_SQLiteClose.name: bBox_SQLiteClose
bBox_SQLiteClose.description: Closes the SQLite3 session created with bBox_SQLiteOpen. Once closed, the reference will be invalid. If the in-memory storage option was used, all SQLite3 data for the session is also dumped.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Session reference returned by bBox_SQLiteOpen

notes: Confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-sqliteclose — an older (pre-1.06, "0.97+"-era) per-function vendor page, parallel to the current wiki but hosted on beezwax.net. Same page format as the wiki (Parameters/Result/Error/Script Step block, First appeared/Examples/Compatibility, prose description).

bBox_SQLiteImport.name: bBox_SQLiteImport
bBox_SQLiteImport.description: Marked "Not Implemented" in the vendor's own bBox Plug-in Demo file reference text — the function name exists and is registered by the plugin, but does not do anything as of 1.06. Do not use.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Session reference (per the vendor's own signature, though the function itself is a no-op)

bBox_DuckDBRun.name: bBox_DuckDBRun
bBox_DuckDBRun.description: Marked "Not Implemented" in the vendor's own bBox Plug-in Demo file reference text. The internal Do_DuckDBRun handler exists in the compiled plugin and the wiki's Script Step List names a "bBox DuckDB Run" script step, but neither a working signature nor behaviour is confirmed. Do not use.

Text and Parsing.notes: Regex, list-comprehension-style iteration, and text-splitting utilities.

bBox_Sort.name: bBox_Sort
bBox_Sort.description: Sorts, or checks whether already sorted, the newline- or null-delimited lines of text. Input can come from the text parameter or a file path given in one of the other parameters. A sortedness check returns error 1 and result "?" if not sorted.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = convert both input/output line endings; 1 = skip CR-to-LF on input; 2 = skip LF-to-CR on output; 3 = don't translate input or output line endings; 4 = don't wait for completion

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to send to sort ("" if not needed, e.g. when sorting a file given via param1)

parameters.name: param1
parameters.description: Sort command option or file path, or "" — named separately in the vendor's own Parameters block even though the header signature folds it into the trailing {; ...}
Additional sort parameters or file paths (optional)

bBox_Sort.result: Sorted values, or the result of a sortedness check
notes: Listed in Home.md's Function List and the third-party draft, but this catalog's original build missed it entirely — no entry existed at all. Signature and description confirmed via both the bBox Plug-in Demo file's embedded reference text and https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-sort (an older, "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page); the two sources agree on everything shown here, including the vendor's own inconsistency between the header signature (folds param1 into {; ...}) and its Parameters block (names param1 separately). Use -k/--key to specify sort key fields, -u/--unique to strip duplicates. See 'man sort' for the full option list.

bBox_Grep.name: bBox_Grep
bBox_Grep.description: Execute a grep command to search text for one or more patterns (basic regular expressions, or extended with -E). For PCRE-style patterns, bBox_JavaScript may be a better fit.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = convert both line endings, wait for output; 1 = skip CR-to-LF on input; 2 = skip LF-to-CR on output; 3 = don't translate input or output line endings

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Input text to be processed (may be "" if passing a file path as one of the parameters)

parameters.name: param1
parameters.description: Normally the search string, but can also contain command option(s) or a file path
Additional parameters (optional)

bBox_Grep.result: Output returned by grep as text
bBox_Grep.script_step_equivalent: bBox Grep [ Text; Option 1; Option 2; Option 3; Option 4 ]
notes: Supports container field references (see shared_reference.container_field_references).
See `man grep` in Terminal for full pattern syntax.

bBox_EvaluateList.name: bBox_EvaluateList
bBox_EvaluateList.description: For each value in a delimited list, apply the given expression and append it to the result — similar to a Python list comprehension, giving a way to loop within a FileMaker calculation.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Delimited list of string values

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: An expression in the same form as FileMaker's native Evaluate function

parameters.name: delimiter
parameters.description: String used as the delimiter, defaulting to a return character. If passed "", each character in values is treated as a separate value

bBox_EvaluateList.error_reference: none — returns "?" as result on error
notes: Two variables are preset during evaluation: $i (current iteration number, starting at 1) and $v (current value in the list, like $values[$i]).

bBox_SplitText.name: bBox_SplitText
bBox_SplitText.signature: bBox_SplitText ( text ; position ; length ; skipRepeats ; separator1 ; separator2 ; delimiter )
bBox_SplitText.description: Returns a version of the source text with the separator(s) replaced by the delimiter — commonly used to "split" text into lines. Only the substring within the given position and length is processed. Unlike Substitute, correctly collapses adjacent separators into one when skipRepeats is set.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Source text

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Index into source text to start the scan

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Index of the last character to scan

parameters.name: skipRepeats
parameters.description: True (1) if no separator should be added when separators are adjacent

parameters.name: separator1
parameters.description: First separator text to use; often a tab or space

parameters.name: separator2
parameters.description: Second separator; often a return/newline

parameters.name: delimiter
parameters.description: Text to substitute in for matching separators

bBox_SplitText.result: Result of the scanned text after substitution
bBox_SplitText.example_code:
bBox_SplitText ($text; 0; 9999; 0; ":"; ¶; ¶)  // replace : and ¶ with ¶, keeping blank lines
bBox_SplitText ($text; 0; 9999; 1; ":"; ¶; ¶)  // same, with skipRepeats collapsing blank lines
bBox_SplitText.doc_bug_note: The live wiki page's parameter list for `text` reads "source texttext: sent to NodeJS' stdin" — the second clause is a copy/paste fragment of bBox_JavaScriptNode's `script` parameter description, not part of bBox_SplitText's own docs. Ignored here; `text` is simply the source text to scan.

bBox_ParsePositionList.name: bBox_ParsePositionList
bBox_ParsePositionList.description: Using a syntax similar to the POSIX `cut` command, converts a field-list expression (numbers, dashes, commas) into a string of "0"/"1" flags indicating which fields were selected. A trailing "+" indicates an open-ended range.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Field expression using numbers, dashes, and commas

bBox_ParsePositionList.result: Result of the scanned text after substitution (a string of 0/1 flags, optionally ending in +)

bBox_GetCharacterStyle.name: bBox_GetCharacterStyle
bBox_GetCharacterStyle.description: Returns the typeface and colour information for the character at a given position in styled text. A position of -1 gives the default text style; a position past the end of text returns the attributes of the last character.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to be examined

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Position of the character to return style information for

bBox_GetCharacterStyle.result: A return-delimited list: font name, font id (per FileMaker client instance), font size, typeface style (comma-delimited text), RGB colour + alpha (comma-delimited text)
bBox_GetCharacterStyle.script_step_equivalent: bBox Get Character Style [ Text; Position ]
notes: For style information across an entire run of text, FileMaker's native GetAsCSS function may be a better fit.
bBox_GetCharacterStyle.doc_bug_note: The live wiki page's Parameters block labels the first parameter `test:` instead of `text:` — a typo in the upstream source, corrected here.

Files and Filesystem.notes: File I/O and metadata functions. All paths are POSIX-format (see shared_reference.file_paths); bBox_FileRead/Write/Status/SymLink have no dedicated wiki pages but are confirmed via the bBox Plug-in Demo file's embedded reference text, and referenced throughout Parameters.md and the Errors table's bBox_File* entry.

bBox_FileRead.name: bBox_FileRead
bBox_FileRead.description: Returns the contents of the file at a POSIX path, for reading into a variable or field. For text data types, the character encoding must be known (typically UTF-8). Input is truncated at 2 GB as a safety measure.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: POSIX path to the file — a literal value; do not escape characters or enclose in quotes

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Result data type: Raw, Best Guess, UTF-8, or UTF-16 (per the demo file's script-step parameter list)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Optional byte offset into the file

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Optional alternate filename for the container result — useful for normalizing file names on import

bBox_FileRead.result: Container reference in the chosen type, or text
notes: since/compatibility/behavioural detail confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-fileread (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page).

bBox_FileWrite.name: bBox_FileWrite
bBox_FileWrite.description: Writes data out to a file at the given POSIX path. The source of data can be either a container reference or text. Set append to true to add to an existing file of the same name rather than overwrite it (be sure the destination folder already exists). Set unzip to true to also write out a decompressed copy if the file is compressed.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Container reference or text to write

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: POSIX destination path — a literal value; do not escape characters or enclose in quotes

parameters.name: append
parameters.description: Optional boolean — true adds to an existing file of the same name

parameters.name: unzip
parameters.description: Optional boolean — true also writes out a decompressed copy if the source is compressed

bBox_FileWrite.result: Number of bytes written (negative on error) — for text, often but not always the same as the character count, since non-ASCII characters may need more than one byte
notes: The original build of this catalog missed the `unzip` parameter entirely, reconstructing this as just `( data ; path {; append} )` — corrected from the demo file's embedded reference text, which shows all four parameters. since/compatibility/result detail confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-filewrite (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page).

bBox_FileStatus.name: bBox_FileStatus
bBox_FileStatus.description: Runs the stat command against the given path to return its size, permissions, and modification times for a file or folder. See 'man stat' in Terminal for the full list of possible parameter options.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: POSIX path to the file or folder — a literal value; do not escape characters or enclose in quotes

parameters.name: parameter
parameters.description: Optional stat parameter — see 'man stat' for the available list

bBox_FileStatus.result: File size, type, POSIX permissions, and access information as given by stat
notes: The first parameter is named filePath in the demo file's own text, not path as this catalog's original reconstruction had it — corrected. since/compatibility confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-filestatus (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page).

bBox_FileSymLink.name: bBox_FileSymLink
bBox_FileSymLink.description: Creates a symbolic link at the destination POSIX path pointing to the source path — equivalent to ln -s in Terminal. Set hardLink to true to create a hard link instead, which is only possible when the source is a file and both paths are on the same volume. Error #17 occurs if the destination already exists.

parameters.name: sourcePath
parameters.description: POSIX source path

parameters.name: destinationPath
parameters.description: POSIX destination path for the new link

parameters.name: hardLink
parameters.description: Optional boolean — true creates a hard link instead of a symlink (files only, same volume only)

notes: The optional third parameter is named hardLink in the demo file's own text, not useHardLink as this catalog's original reconstruction had it — corrected. since/compatibility/behavioural detail (ln -s equivalence, same-volume requirement, error #17 on existing destination) confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-filesymlink (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page). One of the demo's two script-step parameter lists also shows a fourth generic "Parameter" slot whose purpose isn't described anywhere — not included here since its meaning is unconfirmed.

bBox_MimeTypeForPath.name: bBox_MimeTypeForPath
bBox_MimeTypeForPath.description: Returns the MIME type ("IANA media type") inferred for a given file path, e.g. "image/png" for a PNG file path.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: POSIX path to a file

bBox_MimeTypeForPath.result: Mime type, or "" if no file exists at path

Scripting Languages (JavaScript, Node, P.notes: bBox embeds several language runtimes. JavaScript (JavaScriptCore) and Python/Node can expose an `fm` bridge object/class back into FileMaker — see shared_reference.native_fm_bridge. The Python session functions (Compile/Execute/Eval/GetVar/SetVar/Finalize) share ONE process-wide Python VM — see shared_reference.thread_and_session_safety before running them concurrently; bBox_Python3Run is the thread-safe, non-session alternative but cannot use the fm bridge.

bBox_JavaScript.name: bBox_JavaScript
bBox_JavaScript.description: Evaluate one or more JavaScript expressions or statements (complete scripts or a simple calculated result). Each expression has access to globals created by earlier expressions in the same call. Session and thread safe.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The first JavaScript statement or expression

parameters.name: delimiter
parameters.description: Demarcates results for each expression, or a null string. "JSON" as the delimiter (0.86+... actually 1.00+) returns JSON text output directly

parameters.name: param3...param16
parameters.description: Additional JavaScript expressions using the same context (optional)

bBox_JavaScript.result: Output returned by JavaScript as text
bBox_JavaScript.error_reference: bBox_LastError ("js") — session safe, but not thread safe for the error result itself
notes: If multiple expressions are given and delimiter is a null string, only the result of the last expression is returned.
Requires the libjavascriptcoregtk library on Ubuntu (added in bBox 1.00).

"JSON" as the delimiter value avoids needing to JSON-encode output manually in JavaScript, but each expression's output is converted separately and concatenated without additional delimiters when multiple expressions are given.

bBox_JavaScriptNode.name: bBox_JavaScriptNode
bBox_JavaScriptNode.description: Executes a script file (container reference or POSIX path) using FileMaker Server's Node.js environment, rather than JavaScriptCore. Typically server-side only, unless both Pro and Server are installed locally or the alternate-path mode is set. Session and thread safe. Parameters may change in a future version.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 4 = run asynchronously; 16 = use alternate installation path for node executable (0.99.8+); 32 = combine stdout & stderr (useful when debugging); 64 = expand .zip container files, passing the directory path instead (not for the main script parameter)

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Sent to Node's stdin

parameters.name: script
parameters.description: Path or container reference of the main script
Additional parameters for the node command (optional)

bBox_JavaScriptNode.result: Output returned by JavaScript as text
notes: See the Node.js documentation (v22.14 at time of writing) for node's own parameters.

bBox_JQ.name: bBox_JQ
bBox_JQ.description: Evaluate the given JSON text using a jq expression — useful for JSON transformations beyond FileMaker's native JSON functions. On Ubuntu, the jq package must be installed separately (sudo apt install jq).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = convert both line endings; 1 = skip CR-to-LF on input; 2 = skip LF-to-CR on output; 3 = don't translate input or output line endings

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: JSON text to be parsed

parameters.name: param1
parameters.description: First jq option or expression

parameters.name: param3...param16
parameters.description: Additional jq options or expressions (optional)

bBox_JQ.result: Output returned by jq as text
notes: See the jq manual (https://stedolan.github.io/jq/manual/) for operator syntax.
Supports container field references (see shared_reference.container_field_references).

bBox_Ruby.name: bBox_Ruby
bBox_Ruby.signature: bBox_Ruby ( mode ; text ; param1 {; param2 ; ... ; param5} )
bBox_Ruby.description: Executes a script using the Ruby interpreter, analogous to bBox_Bash/bBox_Python3Run.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = convert both line endings; 1 = skip CR-to-LF on input; 2 = skip LF-to-CR on output; 3 = don't translate input or output; 4 = run asynchronously (0.96+); 16 = use alternate path at /usr/local/bin (0.96+)

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Input text to be processed (sent to stdin)

parameters.name: param1
parameters.description: Ruby option (optional)

parameters.name: ...param5
parameters.description: Additional Ruby options (optional, up to param5)

notes: Supports container field references (see shared_reference.container_field_references).

bBox_Python3Run.name: bBox_Python3Run
bBox_Python3Run.description: Runs a Python 3 script in a fresh interpreter invocation each time — a simpler, non-persistent, thread-safe alternative to the Compile/Execute/GetVar/SetVar/Finalize session-based functions. Does not support the fm bridge module.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = convert both line endings, wait for output; 1 = skip CR-to-LF on input; 2 = skip LF-to-CR on output; 3 = don't translate input or output; 4 = run asynchronously; 16 = use alternate Python command path; 32 = combine stdout & stderr

parameters.name: script
parameters.description: Text to be compiled into bytecode

parameters.name: param1...
parameters.description: Optional parameters for the python3 command, retrievable in Python via sys.argv

bBox_Python3Run.script_step_equivalent: bBox Python3 Run [ Mode: Script: Input: Param1: Param2: Param3: ]
notes: Requires the Python Software Foundation's Python on macOS (default path /usr/local/bin/python3, alternate /usr/bin/python3); apt-get on Ubuntu (default /usr/bin/python3, alternate /usr/local/bin/python3).
Add Linux dist-packages paths manually if needed: sys.path.append('/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages').
Use mode 32 while testing/debugging — otherwise Python syntax-error messages sent to stderr are lost and only bBox_LastError's own message remains.
Thread safe — multiple Python 3 scripts can safely run at the same time (unlike the Compile/Execute session functions).

bBox_PythonCompile.name: bBox_PythonCompile
bBox_PythonCompile.description: Initialises the Python environment and compiles the script into bytecode for later execution via bBox_PythonExecute. Only one Python VM exists process-wide (see shared_reference.thread_and_session_safety).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = convert both line endings; 1 = skip CR-to-LF on input; 8 = keep any previous globals; 9 = skip conversion and keep previous globals

parameters.name: script
parameters.description: Text to be compiled and executed later

notes: By default, a previously created but not-yet-finalized Python environment is released (possibly setting an error) when this is called again; add 8 to mode to keep it persistent (e.g. to retain globals from the last execution).

When run via PSoS/schedules, check whether another session is already using the shared Python environment before compiling — only one copy exists at a time. bBox_Python3Run avoids this by spawning separate instances.
Over 30 example Python scripts ship in the bBox Plug-in Demo file.

bBox_PythonExecute.name: bBox_PythonExecute
bBox_PythonExecute.description: Executes the previously compiled Python session code from bBox_PythonCompile. The script's stdout output is returned as the result (e.g. via a print statement); results can also be retrieved afterward with bBox_PythonGetVar, or pushed into a FileMaker table via fm.executesql. If an uncaught Python exception occurs, "?" is returned and bBox_LastError returns the exception text. Call bBox_PythonFinalize when done with the environment.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Line-ending/behaviour flags, shared with other Python-family functions

bBox_PythonExecute.result: stdout output of the executed script, or "?" on an uncaught exception
bBox_PythonExecute.error_reference: bBox_LastError (-3) — not thread or session safe
notes: since/compatibility/behavioural detail (exception handling, output-retrieval options, a future version requiring the bBox_PythonCompile session reference) confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-pythonexecute (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page).

bBox_PythonEval.name: bBox_PythonEval
bBox_PythonEval.description: Evaluates a Python expression or simple function call within an existing session (bBox_PythonCompile must have been called first) and returns the evaluated value.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Session reference — note bBox's own text refers to "bBox_Compile", almost certainly meaning bBox_PythonCompile

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: Python expression or simple function call to evaluate

bBox_PythonEval.error_reference: bBox_LastError (-3) — not thread or session safe
bBox_PythonEval.doc_bug_note: CONFLICTING SOURCES, not resolved: the demo file (1.06-era, three identical occurrences) consistently shows this exact 2-parameter, session-based signature and description above. But https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-pythoneval (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page, since 0.84) describes a materially DIFFERENT, 1-parameter function: `bBox_PythonEval( expression )`, explicitly described as "a shorter, one-shot version of what PythonCompile/PythonExecute/PythonFinalize does" that "invokes Python directly via the Python library" rather than depending on an existing compiled session — no reference parameter at all, error `bBox_LastError ("python")` instead of `(-3)`. These read as two genuinely different function behaviours, not a formatting inconsistency — either the function was changed to add a reference parameter sometime after 0.84, or one source is simply wrong. Kept the demo file's (newer, 1.06) version as primary since it's the more current source, but do not trust either signature without testing directly in FileMaker first.

bBox_PythonGetVar.name: bBox_PythonGetVar
bBox_PythonGetVar.description: Returns the value of a named Python global variable. Defaults to treating it as a string; the type can be specified via bBox_PythonSetVar's asType to avoid unwanted conversion.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Python variable name to return the value of

bBox_PythonGetVar.result: Date, numeric, or text value from the variable
notes: Python globals are released when bBox_PythonFinalize is called, so extract needed values first.
Returns an empty string if the named Python variable does not exist.
A future bBox version may require the session reference ID from bBox_PythonCompile as a parameter.

bBox_PythonSetVar.name: bBox_PythonSetVar
bBox_PythonSetVar.description: Creates or replaces a Python global variable with a given name and value. The preferred way to supply input to a compiled script (Python functions don't support stdin), so call after bBox_PythonCompile but before bBox_PythonExecute.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Python variable name

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Container, numeric, or string value to store in the Python variable

parameters.name: asType
parameters.description: Optional type override: b = Bool, d = Date, f = Float, F = bytearray (container/text file data), i = Integer, m = DateTime, s = String (default, UTF-16)

notes: A future bBox version may require the session reference ID from bBox_PythonCompile as a parameter.
compatibility confirmed via https://www.beezwax.net/bbox-pythonsetvar (an older "0.97+"-era per-function vendor page) — the wiki page itself doesn't state one.

bBox_PythonFinalize.name: bBox_PythonFinalize
bBox_PythonFinalize.description: Releases the current Python environment from memory.
notes: IMPORTANT: only one shared Python VM exists across server-side processes — implement your own locking if PSoS/schedules may overlap. CWP scripts get their own separate copy.
A future version will require the session reference ID from bBox_PythonCompile as a parameter.

Images.notes: GraphicsMagick works cross-platform (with extra Linux dependencies); sips is macOS-only but can leverage hardware acceleration GraphicsMagick can't.

bBox_GraphicsMagick.name: bBox_GraphicsMagick
bBox_GraphicsMagick.description: Executes a gm command to manipulate, compare, or describe image files. Each gm option/value/switch is typically a separate FileMaker parameter.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = wait for output; 4 = run asynchronously (no wait); 32 = combine stdout & stderr

parameters.name: param1, param2, ...
parameters.description: One or more options sent to the gm command

bBox_GraphicsMagick.result: Any text output returned by the gm command
notes: The macOS-bundled version supports: large files (<32-bit), BZIP, JBIG, JPEG, LCMS, PNG, SVG (Ubuntu only), TIFF, ZLIB.
Requires extra installation steps on Ubuntu — see the Installation reference.
See bBox_Sips for a macOS-only alternative that may perform better and support additional formats.

bBox_Sips.name: bBox_Sips
bBox_Sips.description: Performs image conversion/manipulation using macOS's built-in sips tool. macOS only; see bBox_GraphicsMagick for a Linux-compatible alternative (though GraphicsMagick is less likely to leverage hardware acceleration).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 = wait for output; 4 = run asynchronously (no wait); 32 = combine stdout & stderr

parameters.name: param1, param2, ...
parameters.description: One or more options sent to the sips command

bBox_Sips.result: Output returned by the sips command as text
notes: See `man sips` in Terminal for usage details.

Clipboard (Pasteboard).notes: macOS-only. UTI codes identify each clipboard "flavor" (data type) — see Apple's System-Declared Uniform Type Identifiers reference.

bBox_PasteboardFlavors.name: bBox_PasteboardFlavors
bBox_PasteboardFlavors.description: Get all possible data types ("flavors") currently on the system pasteboard, as a return-delimited list. If item is specified, only that item's flavors are returned.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Item index (optional, base 1)

bBox_PasteboardFlavors.result: List of UTI codes for the available flavors
notes: No result if the clipboard is empty or the index is out of range.

bBox_PasteboardGet.name: bBox_PasteboardGet
bBox_PasteboardGet.description: Get data from the user's clipboard as text.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 3 = UTF-8 encoding, don't translate line endings; 4 = expect 2-byte (UTF-16) characters in output

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Item index, usually 1

parameters.name: flavor

bBox_Version.name: bBox_Version
bBox_Version.description: Returns the installed bBox plug-in version, or "?" if bBox is not installed/registered — useful as an install-check before triggering an install step.

notes: The "extended" format matches what Get (InstalledFMPlugins) returns.

bBox_LastError.name: bBox_LastError
bBox_LastError.description: Returns the last error for a given function family/reference. If there is no error, returns "0". On error, many calls return a numeric code as the first value, followed by one or more lines of descriptive message or stack trace. Error codes are not cleared by this call, so it can be called multiple times.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: A session reference (numeric) or a fixed family name (e.g. "posix", "curl") — see shared_reference.error_reference for the full table

notes: Session safe, so it reliably works across multiple simultaneous server-side PSoS/scheduled sessions. Not thread safe except for DuckDB references — recursion or concurrent calls within one session can retrieve the wrong result.
Numeric codes are often identical to the underlying binary's own exit/error code (e.g. bBox_Curl mirrors curl's own result when run in Terminal).
Add 32 to a function's mode value to combine stdout & stderr, surfacing stderr-only error detail (useful when debugging Python).

mode_flags.description: Bit flags shared across many bBox functions/script steps to adjust behaviour. Flags are combinable by addition (e.g. 1+4 = 5). Support varies per function — check the specific function's own mode description before assuming a flag applies; invalid flags are typically ignored rather than erroring. Some function pages describe pre-combined values (0, 1, 2, 3...) as a convenience enum rather than spelling out each bit — e.g. bBox_Shell's "3" is just +1 and +2 combined.

flags.1: Skip conversion of carriage returns to line feeds on input
flags.2: Skip conversion of line feeds to carriage returns on output
flags.32: Combine stdout & stderr (often needed to see error output that doesn't go to stdout)

mode_flags.example: bBox_Zsh (1+4; "/usr/local/mylongrunningscript.sh")  // skip CR-to-LF on input, run asynchronously

error_reference.description: The bBox_LastError(reference) parameter to use per function, from Errors-&-Troubleshooting.md. Two function names in the live wiki table are typoed ("bBob_Javascript", "bBob_JavascriptNode") — corrected below to bBox_JavaScript / bBox_JavaScriptNode.

table.bBox_EvaluateList: N/A — returns "?" as its result on error
table.bBox_MacNotificationsGetSettings: N/A — returns "?" as its result on error
table.bBox_PythonCompile: -3 / N/A — use the reference number from bBox_PythonCompile
table.bBox_PythonExecute: (future versions will use a reference value > 0)

container_field_references.description: Since 0.97, these functions/script steps accept a container field reference directly as a parameter in place of a file path: bBox_Bash (function & script step), bBox_Curl, bBox_GraphicsMagick, bBox_Grep (function & script step), bBox_JavaScriptNode, bBox_JQ, bBox Python3 Run (script step), bBox_Ruby, bBox_Sips, bBox_Zsh (function & script step). The container's file is written to a temp path in the form bBox_file_XXXXXXXXX.bin (always .bin regardless of original type/name; a directory if it's a zip with the unzip mode flag set) and that path is substituted in as the parameter. These temp files are purged by the OS after 3 days or the next reboot — clean up sooner if working with large files, e.g. `find /tmp -type f -mmin +180 -name 'bBox_file_*' -delete` (Ubuntu) or the /private/tmp equivalent on macOS. Older bBox versions used a `bBox_posix_` prefix instead.

file_paths.description: Functions/script steps expecting a path always use POSIX format. Convert a FileMaker path (e.g. from Get(DocumentsFolder)) with FileMaker's native ConvertFromFileMakerPath function before passing it to a bBox function.

type_conversion.description: FileMaker passes bBox data as one of: Binary, Boolean, Date, Invalid, Number, Text, Time, TimeStamp. Non-Text values are frequently converted to their text equivalent before use (e.g. a Numeric 1234 becomes the string "1234" for a shell call). Use bBox_ReferenceInfo to inspect a parameter's native type.

line_endings_and_encoding.description: FileMaker strips literal line breaks from string literals in calculations — always store multi-line scripts in a text field, container field, or insert them via the Insert Text script step. FileMaker itself defaults to Carriage Return line endings; bBox typically auto-translates to/from POSIX newlines unless overridden via the mode flags (+1/+2). POSIX commands generally expect UTF-8 — 16/32-bit Unicode characters that don't map to a UTF-8 equivalent are stripped during conversion.

native_fm_bridge.description: bBox_JavaScript, bBox_JavaScriptNode, bBox_PythonExecute, and bBox_PythonEval can expose an `fm` class/object in the script environment for calling back into FileMaker. Python requires `import fm` first. Parameters are identical across the two languages except fm.executesql (JavaScript takes only the SQL expression; Python also accepts an optional list of bind values) — a future bBox version is expected to align them. DuckDB has an analogous `fmevaluate` SQL function for the same purpose.

methods.fm.evaluate(expression): Evaluates a FileMaker calculation expression, returning the result as a native value in the host language. Can also be used to set FileMaker globals (e.g. Python: fm.evaluate('$$myGlobalName = "text"')) — though this specific form does not work correctly in bBox 1.06.
methods.fm.executesql(expression) [JavaScript]: Runs a FileMaker SQL expression, returning a newline/tab-delimited string of results.
methods.fm.executesql(expression, values=None) [: Runs a FileMaker SQL expression, optionally with bind values, returning a Python list (tuple) of rows — no delimiter characters needed, unlike FileMaker's native ExecuteSQL.
methods.fm.run(filename, scriptname, {parameter}: Runs a FileMaker script in the given file, optionally passing a parameter. Retrieve the script's result afterward with fm.evaluate("Get (ScriptResult)").

thread_and_session_safety.description: "Thread safe": multiple PSoS/schedule sessions can call the function AND multiple unrelated calls can run concurrently within one session (each call is atomic with no shared side effects). "Session safe": each PSoS/schedule session must keep its own context, so concurrent calls are safe across different sessions but NOT safe more than one at a time within a session.

by_function.bBox_LastError: Session safe for most cases; also thread safe for DuckDB references
by_function.bBox_JavaScript: Session and thread safe, but bBox_LastError("JS") is only session safe
by_function.bBox_PythonExecute / bBox_PythonEval: NOT thread or session safe — only one process-wide Python VM exists (Python's GIL); use a mutex/blocking mechanism if calls could overlap
by_function.bBox_Python3Run: Thread safe (spawns a separate interpreter per call); does not support the fm bridge class

psos_and_calculation_field_limits.description: Functions interacting with windows/applications (much of bBox_Applescript) don't work under PSoS/schedules — there's no accessible logged-in GUI session even if a user is nominally logged in. FMS's script engine is also more resource-constrained: heavy native code (e.g. a large Python loop pushing data onto the stack) can exceed stack limits and crash the script engine — the demo file's prime-number generator crashes above ~55,000 in its range. PSoS results are also capped at 1,000,000 characters (FileMaker 14 limit) — exceeding this can hang the client. Shell/Bash/Python/Ruby-family functions do not behave reliably in a STORED calculation field — use unstored calculations instead.
